title: Array Index Access
description: What is the time complexity of accessing an element by index in an array?
explanation: Arrays use base address + offset, so element access is always constant time regardless of array size.

title: LIFO Data Structure
description: Which data structure follows the LIFO principle?
explanation: Last In, First Out — like a stack of plates. The last element pushed is the first to be popped.

title: Linked List Head Pointer
description: What does the 'head' pointer in a singly linked list point to?
explanation: Head always points to the first node of the list; it is null if the list is empty.

title: Linear Search Best Case
description: What is the best-case time complexity of Linear Search?
explanation: Best case: the target element is at index 0, requiring only one comparison.

title: Linear vs Non-Linear Structures
description: Which of the following is NOT a linear data structure?
explanation: Trees are hierarchical (non-linear). Arrays, Stacks, and Queues are all linear data structures.

title: Queue Insertion & Deletion
description: In a queue, insertion happens at ___ and deletion at ___.
explanation: FIFO — enqueue (insert) at the rear, dequeue (delete) from the front.

title: Binary Search Complexity
description: What is the average-case time complexity of Binary Search?
explanation: Binary Search halves the search space at each step. The array must be sorted beforehand.

title: Stable Sorting with O(n log n) Worst Case
description: Which sorting algorithm is stable AND has O(n log n) worst-case time complexity?
explanation: Merge Sort is always O(n log n) in all cases and is stable — it preserves the relative order of equal elements.

title: DFS Space Complexity
description: How much space does recursive DFS on a graph with V vertices use?
explanation: The recursive call stack depth is at most V in the worst case (a linear chain graph).

title: Height of Complete Binary Tree
description: What is the height of a complete binary tree with n nodes?
explanation: Height = ⌊log₂(n)⌋ — it grows logarithmically as each level roughly doubles the node count.

title: BST In-Order Traversal
description: In which traversal of a BST are nodes visited in ascending sorted order?
explanation: In-order traversal (Left → Root → Right) on a BST always produces elements in sorted ascending order.

title: Hash Table Worst Case Insert
description: What is the worst-case time complexity of inserting into a Hash Table with chaining?
explanation: Worst case: all n keys hash to the same bucket, forming a chain of length n — degrading to linear search.

title: Shortest Path in Unweighted Graph
description: Which algorithm finds the shortest path in an unweighted graph?
explanation: BFS explores the graph level by level, guaranteeing the shortest path by edge count in unweighted graphs.

title: Building a Max-Heap
description: What is the time complexity of building a Max-Heap from an unsorted array?
explanation: Floyd's bottom-up heapify is O(n) — most nodes are near the leaves and require only O(1) work each.

title: DP Inapplicability
description: Which problem CANNOT be solved using Dynamic Programming?
explanation: Hamiltonian Path is NP-complete — no known polynomial-time DP solution exists for the general case.
